_: What each landmass of the painted map looks like (owner 2026-10-11) – scripts/map-paint.mjs puts the zones of a region into its prompt. `at` = a point on the island (world units; the landmass under it), `rect` = every landmass whose middle lies inside and that no `at` zone took. Land in no zone gets a season of its own (random, fixed per island). The numbers: logs/map-paint/zones-sheet.png (scripts/map-zones.mjs).

zones.name: desert
zones.look: an African desert like an alien DOOM planet: rust-red and ochre dunes, cracked salt pans, scorched strange rock formations, an unearthly hostile glow

zones.name: altiplano
zones.look: a high steppe like the Peruvian altiplano: golden-olive grass textures, wide plains with low, rounded mountain ranges, lichen and pale stone

zones.name: alps
zones.look: the Alps in deep WINTER (always winter here): snow and ice textures, sharp rocky ridges, glaciers, frozen blue shadows

zones.name: jungle
zones.look: a REPTILE world of dense primeval JUNGLE: scaly and leathery textures, tangled vines and giant leaves, steaming swamp greens, iridescent lizard-skin patterns

zones.name: wasteland
zones.look: a WASTELAND: a post-industrial nuclear disaster zone scarred by fracking – cracked toxic crusts, oily black and sulphur-yellow pools, rusted metal textures, ash and slag, a sickly radioactive green glow

zones.name: archipelago
zones.look: an island world – NOT a city: every small island its own crazy jewel-like texture, like the style reference

seasons: in SPRING: fresh greens, blossoming colour fields, wet earth
in SUMMER: saturated warm colours, dry grass, sun-baked stone
in AUTUMN: rust, amber and crimson, fallen-leaf textures
in WINTER: frost, snow crust and ice, cold blue light
